newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Hernu was not Romanian spy, says defector.
newsitem.headline: France's Hernu was not Romanian spy, says defector.

text.p: Former French Defence Minister Charles Hernu was never a spy for Romania, a Romanian ex-secret service chief was quoted as saying in a French magazine interview released on Wednesday.

The statements by Ion Pacepa, head of Romania's intelligence service (DIE) until he defected to the West in 1978, contradicted reports in the French weekly L'Express that Hernu, worked for the Bulgarian, Romanian and Soviet secret services.
Pacepa told the weekly L'Evenement du Jeudi he believed reports that Hernu was a Communist spy originated with the former Soviet KGB secret service.
Hernu was defence minister from 1981-1985 and died in 1990.
The L'Express story created a sensation with the allegation that Hernu was a spy for at least a decade from 1953.
"The file is a fake. Until I became a political exile in the United States, I never knew anything about any relationship between Hernu and DIE," the magazine quoted Pacepa as saying.

L'Evenement du Jeudi said it interviewed Pacepa by mail at an undisclosed location where he lives under U.S. protection. Pacepa was also quoted as saying that the KGB had sought to pass off deceased Westerners as Communist agents to rehabilitate its own image as the Iron Curtain crumbled.

L'Express had said the late President Francois Mitterrand, Hernu's political patron, was told of the allegations in 1992 by France's DST counter-intelligence service after it received a dossier from east European spy services.
It said the DST took the charges seriously enough to inform Mitterrand but was unable to verify them. Mitterrand ordered the reports to be kept secret, arguing Hernu could not defend himself.
